prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system: potable-water production, automation/manual supervision; boundary River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood)/Raw Water Screen Channel–High Service Pump Header; distribution excluded.

Intake respects withdrawal limits/demand/depth; starts require suction/discharge/motor/valve/safety permissives; low level/drive fault/local control/unproven interlock block; lost permissives alarm/stop. Screen sends Rake Torque Snapshot after cleaning; rapid changes require cleaning/drawdown verification; high-high field confirmation. Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode/targets/responses; normal resumes after approved stability duration. Maintenance Planner schedules poststorm work.

Coagulant Dosing Skid (Marigold) meters coagulant/sends Alum Batch Ticket per lot. Chief Operator sets condition-based dose; trimming requires feedback/targets/verified response. Duty Engineer authorizes temporary rapid-turbidity adjustments pending confirmation; approves configuration/behavior/boundary changes. Lost feedback: last verified safe/approved fixed dose plus grab samples. Sustained ineffectiveness: review strength/pumps/mixing/raw water.

North Filter Gallery (Cobalt) records effluent turbidity/headloss each scan; South Filter Gallery sends Filter Run Exception Note. Runs consider duration/headloss/turbidity/backwash/upstream conditions; postwash return requires target rinse-to-waste/stable turbidity. Laboratory Technician confirms analyzer/sample disagreements.

Manual chemical-feed/valve-sequencing/filter-start-stop overrides only if automation unavailable/inappropriate; document reason, closely monitor, restore promptly. Dose increments small unless Chief Operator approves urgent correction. Chief Operator reviews significant deviations/restored quality; laboratory independently confirms recovery; sets daily sampling priorities.

Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (Sparrow) receives custody-controlled compliance/process samples. Collection labels: location/time/initials/preservation/analyses; Laboratory Technician checks container/holding-time/temperature/preservative/seal before logging. Verify scheduled samples from intake/screen/both galleries/contact basin/header.

Chlorine Contact Basin: particulate carryover affects disinfection; Chlorine Residual Alarm needs immediate assessment. Clearwell Level Controller coordinates storage/filter production. Backwash Recovery Tank recovers. Distribution Dispatcher receives advance production-limit/demand-risk notices; North Distribution Pressure Station/South Distribution Pressure Station influence pumping. Chemical Supplier Driver: verified deliveries; Residuals Hauler: removal. SCADA Historian Server (Lantern) retains trends/doses/analyzers/filter-status/washes/comments; synchronize devices.

Document units:
S083: The Laboratory Technician uses the Alum Batch Ticket to verify chemical lot identity before recording related laboratory observations.
S084: The Laboratory Technician prepares and sends the Sample Chain Slip after verifying that custody entries are complete and legible.
S085: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench sends the Jar Test Photograph Set after the comparison images have been checked for date, time, and sample identifiers.
S086: Lantern must retain accepted laboratory result timestamps with the associated process trend interval so that reconciliation can be repeated during audits.
S087: Field meter readings used for immediate control are treated as provisional until they are compared with laboratory results collected from the same location and time window.
S088: The Laboratory Technician records any mismatch between bottle labels, bench log entries, and operator notes before assigning an acceptance status to the sample.
S089: If a sample is received outside the approved holding time or temperature range, the result may be used for troubleshooting but is not accepted for compliance reporting.
S090: Calibration checks, method blanks, duplicate measurements, and control standards are reviewed before process measurements are released to operations.
S091: Results associated with failed quality checks are flagged, investigated, and either corrected with documented justification or rejected from the accepted data set.
S092: The Duty Engineer reviews significant differences between field readings and laboratory values when those differences could affect chemical feed, filter loading, or disinfection decisions.
S093: For turbidity and particle-related analyses, the Laboratory Technician confirms that sample mixing, settling time, and instrument range are appropriate for the expected raw or filtered water condition.
S094: For disinfectant residual analyses, the Laboratory Technician confirms reagent condition, sample contact time, and measurement timing before accepting the result.
S095: When a Chlorine Residual Alarm is active, related grab samples receive priority handling so that alarm response can be checked against an independent measurement.
S096: The Chief Operator is notified when laboratory confirmation does not support the field indication that caused an operating adjustment.
S097: Accepted laboratory results are reconciled to operating trends by matching collection time, sample point, process state, and recent manual observations.
S098: If Storm Intake Mode changes the character of incoming water, the sampling frequency is increased until raw and settled water measurements show stable behavior.
S099: The Backwash Recovery Tank is sampled after return-to-process events when recovered water quality could influence filter performance or finished water stability.
S100: The Laboratory Technician preserves all custody and acceptance records for review by the Chief Operator, Duty Engineer, and regulatory auditors.
